chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Jahm al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from one of his companions, who said:

I was behind Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) upon al-Safa or upon al-Marwa, and he did not increase upon two words: 'O Allah! I ask You for good expectation of You in every state, and truthfulness of intention in reliance upon You.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk during Sa'i
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, the second hill in the Sa'i ritual
key_terms.حُسْنَ الظَّنِّ: Good expectation or opinion of God

ai.seo_question: What was the specific supplication recited by Imam Musa al-Kazim during Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights Imam Musa al-Kazim’s (peace be upon him) practice of offering a concise yet profound supplication while standing between Safa and Marwa, the site of the Sa'i ritual commemorating Hajar’s search for water. The Imam’s choice of words underscores the Shia emphasis on Husn al-Zann (optimistic trust in God) and Sidq al-Niyyah (sincerity of intention) as the core spiritual dispositions required during acts of worship, transforming the physical act of Sa'i into a journey of the heart.
